text.p: The following the are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Fares for most forms of public transport will go up in June and commuters can expect small increases on a regular basis, the Public Transport Council said.
- The Singapore Institute of Management will be turned into a private university specialising in finance and business courses, said Deputy Prime Minister Tony Tan said.
- Government-linked Singapore Technologies Industrial Corporation has joined Asian movie giant Golden Harvest in a joint venture to invest in China's cinemas.
- Market talk that Malaysian-listed Hospital Pantaiwill sell its 20 percent stake in Parkway Holdings pushed both counters to record highs in the stock exchange.
- The President and 15 board members at Nomura Securities Co Ltd in Japan resigned to take responsibility for a racketeering scandal that has sullied the name of Japan's biggest securities firm.

- Nomura Securities President Masashi Suzuki and 15 other board members quiet from Japan's biggest securities brokerage to take collective responsibility for the firm's illegal share deals and its involvement with racketeers.
- The Public Transport Council has decided to deregulate with immediate effect surcharges taxi operators levy for phone bookings and premier services.
- Shares of Singapore Telecom have slid 36 cents, or 12 percent, since it lost part of its monopoly this month and analysts said it may be a good time to accumulate the share.
- First Capital Corp has teamed up with Sathorn Thani Company Ltd to form a joint venture company for property development and related activities in Thailand.
- Taiwanese President Lee Teng-hui said the time and conditions for starting full-scale direct transport links between Taiwan and China were not yet in place.

- The Hong Kong Shipowners' Association hopes to sign an agreement shortly on the questions of flags flown by Hong Kong and Taiwanese ships flown in each other's ports after Beijing takes over the British colony in June, a spokesman said.
